newsitem.title: PERU: Rebels did not recognize Fujimori's hostage brother.
newsitem.headline: Rebels did not recognize Fujimori's hostage brother.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori's younger brother Pedro was not recognised by his Marxist rebel captors for 10 days in Peru's hostage crisis, a government source said on Friday.
"They only found out it was Pedro Fujimori when his name began to figure in local media as one of the hostages," said a senior government official, who asked not to be named.
Fujimori's mother and sister were also among the more than 500 guests at a Japanese embassy cocktail party stormed by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels 24 days ago.
They too were apparently not recognised by the rebels and freed within hours with all the women and elderly captives.
Pedro Fujimori is among 74 VIP hostages the MRTA is still holding at the residence as bargaining chips to obtain the release of their roughly 400 jailed comrades.
The source said the captives were suffering from the lack of running water and electricity, and some had stomach problems. "It's a desperate situation," he said.
Supreme Court President Moises Pantoja was in the worst conditional mentally, the source added. "He's trembling, very afraid of what might happen."
The two government ministers still inside, however, were showing "an iron will" and were determined to leave last after assuring all their fellow captives were out.
"(Foreign Minister) Francisco Tudela is extraordinarily strong. He said: 'I want to go out last. Tell the president not to worry about me at all. I'm fine'."
